blogs.title: Beyond Valuable Information: Construing the Property Element of Fraud Statutes After Ciminelli
blogs.description: Analyze how *United States v. Constantinescu* applies the Supreme Court's rejection of the 'right-to-control' theory in *Ciminelli* to distinguish between mere economic information and actionable property interests in securities fraud cases. This post explores the doctrinal boundary where digital information meets traditional property requirements for conviction.

blogs.title: The Death of the 'Loss' Requirement: Integrating Kousisis Into 5th Circuit Fraud Jurisprudence
blogs.description: Examine the implications of the 5th Circuit's decision to fully adopt the *Kousisis* 'fraudulent-inducement' theory, which mandates no actual pecuniary harm to victims. We break down how this ruling criminalizes schemes where defendants profit through deception even if victims receive securities of market value, fundamentally shifting the lens of intent to defraud.

blogs.title: Pumping the Indictment: Prosecutorial Strategy for Social Media Securities Fraud
blogs.description: Focus on the practical implications of *Constantinescu* for white-collar prosecutors targeting 'pump and dump' schemes operated by social media influencers. Discuss how the court's emphasis on specific allegations of fraudulently inducing purchases (as opposed to vague deprivation of knowledge) reshapes the drafting standards for future securities fraud charges in the digital age.
